character_images_needed: Old Lady (transparent stomach, Simms Taback style)
notes: This is a cumulative repetitive book — ideal for AAC use as students can anticipate and sequence the animals in order. The 11 fringe words prioritise the six swallowed animals (fly, spider, bird, cat, dog, cow, horse — note horse is 7th animal and causes her death) plus the key actions and punchline vocabulary. 'Belly' supports pointing to the stomach visual common in illustrated versions. 'Dead' is intentionally included as the story's repeated dark-humour punchline is highly memorable and motivating for students. Some editions also include a duck or goat — if using those editions, consider swapping 'belly' or 'dead' for the additional animal. The author credit varies widely; Simms Taback's Caldecott-winning 1997 version is most common in classrooms.
